violations.text: No person in charge (with a certificate from a food safety managers course) was present as needed at the time of inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety with RIDOH Center for Food Protection at all times when time temperature control for safety (TCS) food is being prepared, handled, and/or served. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

Raw animal foods (such as chicken, beef, and eggs) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as cooked chicken and raw veggies) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Foods were relocated to the proper areas at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

The food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils were not sanitized at the bar dishwasher. The required utensil surface temperature of 160 degrees Fahrenheit was not achieved during the sanitizing cycle of the dishwasher as evidenced by the failure of the thermolabel (temperature indicator) affixed to the surface of a utensil to turn black. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

Various food items were observed held at 75-94 degrees Fahrenheit under the heating lamps. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Foods were moved to walk-in cooler and/or reheated for service. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

Various food items observed held at 70 degrees Fahrenheit in ambient air temperature. Per staff, foods were taken out of walk-in cooler 2 hours prior to inspection. All foods moved to the walk-in cooler to rapidly cool. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

Various food items were observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

Employees' medicines were not stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, or utensils. Personal items were relocated to areas to prevent possible contamination. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Chicken was observed cooling in containers deeper than 4 inches. Food was moved to shallow pans and placed in the walk-in cooler. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

The following was observed improperly stored: 1) Knives were stored in-between the prep unit and the prep table at the cookline 2) Scoops for rice were observed in stagnant water 3) Containers were used as scoops in dry ingredients All utensils were relocated to proper storage areas. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026
The facility is lacking thermo labels or similar internal temperature indicating device for the dish machine at the bar and kitchen. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

The following was observed of non-food contact surfaces: 1) The cooking equipment was observed with an accumulation of grease 2) The hood ventilation systems were observed with an accumulation of dust and grease 3) The interior and exterior of all the refrigeration units were observed with an accumulation of food debris New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

The following was observed of the physical facilities: 1) The floors in the cookline area have an accumulation of soil residue and food debris. 2) The ceiling vents in the kitchen were observed with an accumulation of dust.3) The walls in the food prep area were observed with an accumulation of food debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

An open employees' beverage container was observed stored in a food preparation area. Employees shall not drink from open beverage containers in order to prevent contamination of their hands, the container, and exposed food. Proper storage for drinking and eating reviewed at time of inspection. Staff removed open beverage containers away from food prep area during inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/14/2024

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (can opener, slicer, knives) were observed with an accumulation of food debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Proper cleaning instructions for food contact surfaces reviewed. Staff removed can opener and knives to 3 bay sink to wash, rinse and sanitize. Slicer was also washed, rinsed and sanitized at time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/14/2024

Employees' medicines were observed stored in the food prep area. Employee's medications shall be stored away from food prep area. -Staff removed the medications during this inspection and stored it in a different location. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/14/2024

Employee beverages were observed stored in direct contact with ice in ice machine. Proper storage of employees' beverages (personal belongings) reviewed. Staff removed the beverages from ice machine and voluntary disposed of ice. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/14/2024

Bowls are being used as scoops in containers of sauces. Utensils used to dispense non-time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods such as sugar and flour must be stored in the food item with their handles above the top of the food within the container. -Staff disposed of the bowls during this inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/14/2024

Employees' clean uniforms were observed stored in the bathroom. Establishment shall not store uniforms in the bathroom to prevent exposure to contamination. -Staff removed the uniforms from the bathroom during this inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 11/14/2024
Ice buildup observed on the walk-in freezer door, preventing door from closing properly. Ice buildup must be removed and freezer shall be monitored. New Violation. Correct By: 11/28/2024

The non-food contact surfaces of the interior of refrigeration units, the ceilings above food prep sink, and racks in the walk-in cooler have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The non-food contact surfaces shall be cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup of residue. New Violation. Correct By: 11/21/2024
The plumbing under the sink attached to the dish machine in the kitchen area was in poor repair (observed leaking). Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023

Bags of corn starch, flour, and sugar were observed adulterated due to rodent gnawing and/or contact with rodent droppings/urine. PIC voluntarily disposed of food. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/28/2023

The presence of rodents is not controlled as evidenced by an accumulation of rodent droppings observed in the back storage area and adulterated food. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests must be controlled by routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests, using acceptable methods to control pests, eliminating harborage conditions, and routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies. PIC to increase pest control service to every two weeks until pest issue is resolved. New Violation. Correct By: 12/28/2023
The plumbing under the sink attached to the dish machine in the kitchen area was in poor repair (observed leaking). Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023

The floor in the back storage area has an accumulation of pooling soil residue, food debris, and rodent droppings. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/28/2023

Rice and crab rangoon, which were prepared in advance, were not cooled to 70 degrees Fahrenheit in 2 hours and then to 41 degrees Fahrenheit within 4 hours. PIC voluntarily disposed of food. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/14/2023

Several foods throughout the walk-in cooler were observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/14/2023

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Rice and crab rangoon were observed stored in containers deeper than four inches and tightly covered. Establishment to train staff on proper cooling methods, managers to monitor temperatures, and cooling logs must be kept for all product at this time. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/14/2023
The plumbing under the sink attached to the dish machine in the kitchen area was in poor repair (observed leaking). Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023
The Person in charge did not assure compliance with critical code requirements. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety at all times when time temperature control for safety (TCS) food is being prepared, handled, and/or served. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

Several open employees' beverage containers were observed stored in a food preparation area. Employees shall not drink from open beverage containers in order to prevent contamination of their hands, the container, and exposed food. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

A red sani-bucket, tongs, metal handles from buckets, and wire scrubbing pads were observed in the hand-washing sinks throughout the kitchen areas. A hand-washing sink must not be used for purposes other than hand washing. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

Raw animal foods were not stored properly to prevent cross-contamination in the walk-in cooler. Except when combined as ingredients, different types of raw animal foods must be separated from each other during storage by using separate equipment or arrranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

The following food contact surfaces were observed with an accumulation of debris: 1) The ice machine had an accumulation of biofilm. PIC voluntarily disposed of ice 2) The slicer had an accumulation of food debris. Staff sanitized equipment 3) The can opener had an accumulation of food debris. Staff sanitized equipment 4) Scoops and meat cleavers were stored soiled. Staff sanitized utensils Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

The quaternary ammonium concentration in the sanitizing solution of the 3-bay sink was 0 parts per million (ppm). According to the manufacturer's use directions, the concentration of the quaternary ammonium must be 200-400 ppm. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

Chicken, eggrolls, and dumplings which were previously cooked and cooled, was only reheated to 100-120 degrees Fahrenheit for hot holding. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding must be reheated to 165 degrees Fahrenheit or above for 15 seconds. PIC voluntarily disposed of food. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

White rice, which was prepared in advance, was not cooled to 70 degrees Fahrenheit in 2 hours and then to 41 degrees Fahrenheit within 4 hours. PIC voluntarily disposed of food. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

Eggrolls, chicken, dumplings, and shrimp were observed held at 55-70 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. PIC voluntarily disposed of food. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

Several foods throughout the walk-in cooler were observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Chicken was observed cooling in large plastic containers greater than four inches deep and rice was observed in large bowl tightly covered with plastic wrap and another large bowl stacked on top. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

The PIC could not provide a thermometer to test food temperatures at time of inspection. Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and be readily accessible for checking cooking, cooling, reheating, and hot/cold holding temperatures of time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. New Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023

The presence of rodents is not controlled as evidenced by an accumulation of rodent droppings in the back food storage area. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests must be controlled by routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests, using acceptable methods to control pests, eliminating harborage conditions, and routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023
Several boxes of food were observed stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

The following utensils were observed stored incorrectly between uses:1) Knives were stored in unclean surfaces between prep unit and table2) Several large rice spoons were store in stagnant water Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023

Cups are being used as scoops in containers of dry ingredients/sauces. Utensils used to dispense non-time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods such as sugar and flour must be stored in the food item with their handles above the top of the food within the container. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023
Staff were observed not changing gloves between changing of tasks. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 12/07/2023
The PIC could not provide test strips to measure the concentration of the quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution for the three bay sink. New Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023
The facility is lacking thermo labels or similar internal temperature indicating device for the dish machines. New Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023
The plumbing under the sink attached to the dish machine in the kitchen area was in poor repair (observed leaking and kept up with string) New Violation. Correct By: 12/21/2023

The ceiling and vents in the main prep line and in the walk-in cooler have an accumulation of soil residue, dust, and biofilm. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 12/14/2023
